parameters.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples before sale, at least annually thereafter, and after a material design change. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% per model. Manufacturers must submit per-model results, sample sizes, and corrective-action plans to regulators, and disclose each model’s test results and failure rate to customers who buy that model. A failure rate above 5% is non-compliant and triggers regulator-supervised corrective action and retesting; it does not by itself prohibit sales or require a recall.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples before sale, at least annually thereafter, and after a material design change. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% per model. Manufacturers must submit per-model results, sample sizes, and corrective-action plans to regulators, and disclose each model’s test results and failure rate to customers who buy that model. A failure rate above 5% is non-compliant and triggers regulator-supervised corrective action and retesting; it does not by itself prohibit sales or require a recall.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples before sale, at least annually thereafter, and after a material design change. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% per model. Manufacturers must submit per-model results, sample sizes, and corrective-action plans to regulators, and disclose each model’s test results and failure rate to customers who buy that model. A failure rate above 5% is non-compliant and triggers regulator-supervised corrective action and retesting; it does not by itself prohibit sales or require a recall. Regulators may impose proportionate restrictions where evidence shows an unacceptable safety risk.

parameters.quote: If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, provide interim precautions, and initiate a mandatory recall of that model. The recall must promptly reach affected customers and use an effective corrective action, such as regulator-approved repair or replacement.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, provide interim precautions, and initiate a mandatory recall of that model. The recall must promptly reach affected customers and use an effective corrective action, such as regulator-approved repair or replacement.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must give customers clear safety notices describing material hazards, safe installation and use, warning signs, and steps to take during an emergency, and promptly update notices when new material risks emerge. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers and the regulator when a model presents a credible safety risk, with specific precautions and support instructions. Manufacturers must report model-level thermal incident rates to regulators and investigate elevated rates. If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, provide interim precautions, and initiate a mandatory recall of that model. The recall must promptly reach affected customers and use an effective corrective action, such as regulator-approved repair or replacement. Affected units must not return to service until the regulator verifies that the remedy adequately addresses the risk.

judge_section_notes: The final rules combine strict incident reporting (24h regulator, 72h customer), a 55 °C/5% thermal test with per-model customer disclosure but no automatic sales stop above the limit, a 6-year retrofit deadline with a feasibility alternative, built-in fire suppression at 36 months, and a mandatory model-specific recall at 8 incidents/100,000/year. All four red lines are satisfied: no public per-model publication, retrofit at 6 years, disclosure to purchasers, and suppression at 36 months. The main asymmetry is that Northwind's Hearth 10 exceeds the 5% test limit but avoids a sales ban, while Halcyon's Ember 8 exceeds the 8/100k recall trigger and is subject to mandatory recall.
